title: Split the oversized scheduler root execution surface
description: Prerequisite for publishing the already-landed provider-slot release transition to the daemon. Measured at HEAD c1ab42b: `packages/scheduler/src/index.ts` is 430 physical lines, beyond the binding split-before-400 cap. It currently curates authority, resource, budget and fairness value/type exports inline. Move that execution-facing export group into one focused root-reachable surface module and have index.ts forward it, without changing the `@moe/scheduler` namespace. Deliverable is a behavior-free barrel split that leaves both production files <=250 lines and makes a later two-file task able to add `releaseProviderSlot` without editing an oversized source. Consumer: the provider-slot root-publication task created immediately after this task, then the daemon release-state composition task and task-e62e3828df234c66969a99b8223487f4.
definitionOfDone: `packages/scheduler/src/index.ts` forwards an exact-LF root-reachable execution-surface module containing the moved authority/resource/budget/fairness exports; the runtime namespace remains byte-for-byte the same reviewed 94-name set and no new capability is published.
`index.ts` and the new production TypeScript surface are each <=250 physical lines; the new `.js` bridge is exactly one LF-terminated export line.

The existing scheduler index-surface suite passes unchanged and a compiled bare-specifier probe from apps/daemon imports representative moved values and types from `@moe/scheduler`, typechecks exit 0, and is deleted in the same command.
A mutation removing one moved forwarding export reddens the named production root-roster assertion; restoring it returns the focused suite green.
`pnpm --filter @moe/scheduler typecheck` and `pnpm --filter @moe/scheduler test` run separately, with a nonzero test-count line and no owned-path regression.
taskRails: Own only packages/scheduler/src/index.ts and a new focused execution-surface `.ts` plus exact one-line LF `.js` bridge; do not edit index-surface.test.ts or change the public namespace.
Pure export move only: no reducer, vocabulary, contract, behavior, package manifest or lockfile change.
Preserve foreign work; TDD/mutation against the existing production root surface; explicit owned-path commit.

implementationPlan.note:
GATE GREEN AS TWO SEPARATE LEGS, AND COMMITTED. DoD 5 met.

LEG 1, on its own, exit captured on its own: `pnpm --filter @moe/scheduler typecheck` -> `tsc --project tsconfig.json`, TYPECHECK_EXIT=0.
LEG 2, on its own: `pnpm --filter @moe/scheduler test` -> `vitest run --root ../.. packages/scheduler/src`, TEST_EXIT=0, `Test Files 45 passed (45)` / `Tests 1411 passed (1411)`.

THE LEG IS PROVEN TO HAVE EXECUTED, not merely to have exited 0. `pnpm --filter <pkg> <script>` prints "No projects matched the filters" and exits 0 for a package that does not resolve, so exit code alone is worthless here. Measured both discriminators explicitly: COUNT_LINE_PRESENT=1 (a `Test Files N passed` line is there) and NO_PROJECTS_MATCHED=0 (that string never appeared). The counts are IDENTICAL to the step-1 baseline, 45 files and 1411 tests — a pure export move must not change how many tests ran, and it changed neither.

COMMIT 3c4c470, BY EXPLICIT PATHSPEC OVER EXACTLY THE THREE OWNED PATHS. `git show --stat`:
  packages/scheduler/src/execution-surface.js |   1 +
  packages/scheduler/src/execution-surface.ts | 203 +++++

Nothing else rode along. The index was empty of peer staging when I staged (`git diff --cached --name-only` was blank beforehand), so no foreign file could have been captured. The two untracked new files needed an explicit `git add` first — a pathspec-limited `git commit` alone commits NOTHING for a path git does not yet track, and would have silently produced a commit containing only index.ts.

COMMITTED BYTES VERIFIED FROM THE OBJECT STORE, not from the working copy: `git show HEAD:packages/scheduler/src/execution-surface.js | od -c` = `export * from "./execution-surface.ts";\n`, 40 bytes, terminating `\n` with no `\r`. That matters because `.gitattributes` sets `* text=auto eol=lf` and normalises on checkout, so a working-tree read can look right while the stored blob differs; reading the blob is the only check that settles DoD 2's "exactly one LF-terminated export line".

`git status --porcelain -- packages/scheduler/` is empty after the commit: nothing of mine is left uncommitted, and no scratch, probe or evidence file survives anywhere in the tree (the apps/daemon probe was deleted inside the same command that ran it, back in step 4).

TOOLING NOTE FOR THE NEXT AGENT, cost me one failed attempt: `git commit -- <paths> -m "msg"` does NOT work. Everything after `--` is parsed as pathspec, so git rejected each `-m` and each message string with "error: pathspec '-m' did not match any file(s) known to git" and made no commit at all. Message flags must precede the `--` separator. It fails loudly rather than committing the wrong thing, but the error text points at pathspecs and reads like a missing-file problem.

HEAD moved twice more under me during this step (fbbabda -> d60a48f -> my 3c4c470); peers are landing continuously in this shared tree. Verified before staging that d60a48f touched only `apps/daemon/src/planning/active-graph-projection.ts` and nothing of mine.

The plan says this drill shows something "the sorted NAME list alone cannot see". It does not. `export type` ERASES the runtime binding, so the name vanishes from `Object.keys` and the name-list assertion reddens too — 2a is behaviourally indistinguishable from drill 1 and proves nothing extra about export KIND.
